editorial.headline: Private Technical Education, with a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: A private technical-education activity open across business scales, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Private technical education is a broad, practical category for privately delivered learning and course services in technical fields. Its scope reaches from design, graphic design and interior design to electronics, engineering, electrical installation, construction, welding, automotive mechanics, surveying, petroleum, building design, research, industrial engineering, marine engineering, mechanical engineering, civil engineering, heavy-equipment technology, mobile-phone and computer technician training, and telecommunications. It also expressly includes education and training services in electricity-related fields. The common thread is applied technical capability: instruction directed toward the skills, systems and disciplines that make technical work possible.

Providers may operate under the activity at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. That matters because the category is not confined to a particular size of provider: the record allows it across the full stated range of business scales. A private operator can therefore frame its educational offering around technical courses and training without the scope being limited to one narrow discipline. The breadth of the listed subjects gives the activity a substantial practical range, while its identity remains clear—private provision of technical education and training.

At the national level, foreign investment is **TERBUKA**, and foreign ownership may reach **100%**. At the national level, the record allows full foreign ownership. The stated national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lesser foreign-share ceiling in the record to qualify that national position.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, island-wide and permanently. For this activity, however, the record states that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. Its Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**: an honest signal that Bali is not closed to PMA registration for this activity under the stated moratorium rule, while the risk classification at Besar scale remains material to the picture. The conclusion is straightforward: this is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not barred for PMA registration in Bali by that moratorium.
